command_or_fixture: Read server_impl.py lines 2050-2080 and 2155-2162 and memory_handlers.py 1629-1720 against spec Requirements 1-2 and AC-4.
counterexample_or_failure_condition: An implementer following Requirement 1 literally holds the WAL read transaction across query embedding; AC-4 still passes.
expected: Spec puts every model call, including the query embedding, outside the snapshot, and AC-4 asserts snapshot_active is False in both the embedding stub and the reranker stub.
known_bad_detection_method: Read-only trace: memory_handlers._memory_query_records -> WaveIndex._memory_candidate_scores (server_impl.py 2155) -> _embed_query (2050); compared against spec Requirements 1-2 and AC-4. No test was run (inferred), so test_ran is false.
limitations: Read-only analysis; no probe run. docs_search already embeds inside its snapshot (pre-existing), so impact is bounded lock duration, WAL growth and Windows file-replacement delay, not data exposure.
observed: Requirement 1 includes the embedding call inside the snapshot; Requirement 2 forbids it; AC-4 checks only the reranker.
proposition: Requirement 1 places index._memory_candidate_scores inside read_snapshot, but that method calls self._embed_query (server_impl.py 2155-2158 -> 2050), which may cold-load the docs embedding model or call the Tensorwell service. That runs model inference while the memory path holds an SQLite read transaction, which Requirement 2 forbids. AC-4 only probes the reranker, so the violation passes every AC.
safety_and_authorization: No repo edits; no memory records touched; no wf_memory_eval run.

disposition_rationale: Two must-requirements contradict and the AC cannot catch it. Fix in the spec: compute the query vector before entering read_snapshot (split embedding out of _memory_candidate_scores or pass a vector), and extend AC-4 to record snapshot_active in the query-embedding stub.

counterexample_or_failure_condition: An implementation that satisfies Requirement 1 literally holds an SQLite read transaction through query embedding (about 40 s on a first CoreML compile) while AC-4 passes; an implementation that embeds before _ensure_loaded on a cold index caches a full-precision embedder against an INT8 index for the life of the process.
expected: The spec names one consistent boundary for query embedding relative to the snapshot, keeps the embedder's precision selection after _ensure_loaded, and an AC can fail when embedding runs inside the snapshot.
known_bad_detection_method: Read-only trace: _memory_query_records -> WaveIndex._memory_candidate_scores (server_impl.py 2155) -> _embed_query (2050) -> _get_embedder (1944, 1990-1993, self._meta precision selection and self._embedders cache), compared against spec Requirements 1-2 and AC-4. The embedding claim was not run (inferred), so test_ran is false. Separately, a throwaway store copy set to building confirmed the root cause (no snapshot: semantic_index_unavailable; snapshot: hybrid_rrf) and the stale-hash guard.
limitations: The embedding-inside-snapshot and precision-mismatch claims are from code read, not executed; the 40 s figure is from a code comment. Corroborates 248lb-sec-query-embed-inside-snapshot and adds the repair constraint.
observed: Code read: _memory_candidate_scores embeds before dense_path_scores; _get_embedder reads self._meta model_versions and caches in self._embedders. Supporting probe: no snapshot gave semantic_index_unavailable; inside read_snapshot gave 5 records with hybrid_rrf; an edited record inside the snapshot gave memory_source_state_stale.
proposition: Requirement 1 places index._memory_candidate_scores, which calls _embed_query, inside read_snapshot, contradicting Requirement 2 (no model inference inside the read transaction); AC-4 stubs only the reranker so it cannot detect this; and the obvious repair (embed before the snapshot) is unsafe on a cold WaveIndex because _get_embedder chooses query precision from self._meta, which _ensure_loaded fills, and caches the choice in self._embedders.
safety_and_authorization: Read-only review; probes ran only on a scratchpad copy; no repository file, memory record or index was modified.

disposition_rationale: Spec fix before readiness: either (a) _ensure_loaded in a first snapshot, embed outside it, then a second snapshot for _ensure_loaded and dense_path_scores, with AC-4 extended to the embedding stub and server_impl.py added to Serialization Points if _memory_candidate_scores is split; or (b) narrow Requirement 2 to the reranker and accept the first-call cost explicitly.

command_or_fixture: .wavefoundry/work/248lb/review/architecture-reviewer-focused-r2.md
counterexample_or_failure_condition: the approval predates an affected repair or is not independently grounded
expected: the approving actor independently verifies the current affected scope
known_bad_detection_method: Refuted plan claim control: the probe showed dense_path_scores does not detect a docs model change between snapshots (the known-bad the recheck must catch), and the second _ensure_loaded exposes the changed identity; grep confirmed the three passages currently state a closed three-tool list, the round-1 defect the spec now covers.
limitations: Readiness review of an unimplemented plan. Non-blocking advisories for the implementer: (1) the three passages say partial reads use one SQLite read transaction; memory_search uses two, so its addition must say so; (2) _attach_partial_index_coverage derives source from data.fallback_reason and data.search_mode while memory nests them under data.retrieval, so a memory fallback during a build would report source stored_rows; the implementer should decide whether memory fallbacks during a build carry the advisory and with which source, and record it in the Progress Log.
observed: Repaired 2475t plan is architecturally sound. The two-snapshot sequence (load, embed with no snapshot, dense read in a second snapshot, rerank outside both) keeps each SQLite read transaction short and inference in the handler; the probe showed snapshot_active False between contexts. The second-snapshot model recheck is necessary and correctly placed in the handler: on a scratch index copy, a model-change between snapshots made _ensure_loaded reload (generation 6381 to 6382) and expose the new docs model_versions, while dense_path_scores returned without error, so the source-hash check alone would miss it. AC-12 reuses _attach_partial_index_coverage, giving the same index_coverage/diagnostic shape as docs_search, code_search and code_ask. All three closed-list passages are planned with four tools. test_memory_records.py baseline: 245 tests OK.
proposition: architecture-reviewer approves the current affected scope
safety_and_authorization: Local review evidence only; no external side effects.

command_or_fixture: python3 -B scratchpad/sec-r2/p2.py <abs scratch root>: a scratch copy of the repo index and memory records; stub embedder and reranker each record sqlite_vector_store.snapshot_active and sleep 0.5 s; read_snapshot wrapped to time each hold. Arm B2: planned structure (handler load in snapshot 1, embed outside, _ensure_loaded plus dense_path_scores in snapshot 2, rerank outside). Arm C: a hook between snapshots rewrites the docs model_versions entry.

expected: A: embed and rerank active True, hold >= 1 s. B: semantic_index_unavailable. B2: hybrid_rrf, both stubs False, each hold in milliseconds. C: fallback, no results.
known_bad_detection_method: Arm A reproduces the round-1 defect (both stubs see an active snapshot, 1.3 s hold); arm B reproduces AC-1's fail-closed control.
limitations: The probe simulates the planned structure by patching _memory_candidate_scores and _ensure_loaded; the split is not implemented yet. AC-4's reranker stub replaces _get_memory_reranker, so it would not detect a cold reranker model construction placed inside snapshot 2; advisory only, current code already calls _get_memory_reranker after the dense read. The model-identity recheck should compare against a value captured in a local at the first load, not re-read from index._meta, which other threads can reload.
observed: A: n=5, embed_active=True, rerank_active=True, hold 1.317 s (the finding reproduced). B: fallback semantic_index_unavailable. B2: n=5, method hybrid_rrf, embed_active=False, rerank_active=False, holds 0.0036/0.0002/0.0036/0.0002/0.0064 s. C: res None, fail closed (reason memory_candidate_state_unavailable from the probe's own exception path; the spec requires the implementer to map it to semantic_index_unavailable). grep: the only production read_snapshot caller is server_impl._partial_index_read (docs_search, code_search, code_ask); no production path calls memory_search inside an outer snapshot, so the ContextVar nesting cannot silently make the inner snapshots no-ops.
proposition: The repaired 2475t plan runs the query embedder and the reranker with no read snapshot active, and holds each snapshot only for a metadata load or one dense read.
public_path: memory_handlers._memory_query_records on a real WaveIndex over a scratch copy of the real index.sqlite in state 'building' (the memory_search handler path).
safety_and_authorization: Scratch copy only; no repo edits; no run_tests; read-only MCP inspection.

disposition_rationale: The repair moves both inference calls outside every snapshot and AC-4 asserts it for both stubs; the executed probe confirms the planned structure holds snapshots for milliseconds and the round-1 shape does not. The finding is resolved for readiness.
